Manx: Ea 5. Yn Fer-ynsee Cadlagh
Vershion s’doillee
Boallagh fer-ynsee schoill snap beg dy chadley y ghoaill gagh fastyr sy çhamyr-
vrastyl. Tra ren ny schoillaryn fenaght jeh cre hon v’eh jannoo shoh, dooyrt eh dy
row eh goll gys Çheer ny Hashlishyn dy veeiteil rish shenn gheiney-creeney.
Fastyr dy row, er laa erskyn towse çheh, huitt paart jeh ny schoillaryn hene nyn
gadley sy çhamyr-vrastyl. Tra va’n fer-ynsee troiddey roo, dooyrt ad:
“Agh vainshter, hie shin dy loayrt rish ny shenn gheiney creeney ayns Çheer ny
Hashlishyn.”
“Dy firrinagh?” vrie yn fer-ynsee lesh pooar jeu. “As cre dooyrt ad?”
“Denee shin row fer-ynsee schoill çheet gys shen gagh fastyr, agh dooyrt ad nagh row
ad rieau er vakin lhied y phersoon."
No 5. The Sleepy Teacher
More difficult version
A school teacher was wont to have a nap every afternoon in the classroom. When the
students asked him why he did this he said that he went to the Land of Visions to meet
old wise masters.
One afternoon, on an exceedingly hot day, some of the students themselves fell asleep
in the classroom. When the teacher was telling them off, they said:
“But sir, we went to talk with the old wise masters in the Land of Visions.”
“Indeed?” the teacher demanded. “And what did they say?”
“We asked if a school teacher came there every afternoon, but they said they’d never
seen any such person.”
